messages:
julia: FYI bringing up harpoon14b-v2 (community fork) on int4 canary. seeing intermittent OOMs on long chats and a small quality dip after quant. memory fragmentation spikes in host logs. anyone seen this pattern? @sam @mike :thinking:

sam: saw something similar on a different model. quick mitigations to try: lower default gen tokens, drop batch_size, and enable tiny slot reservation. e.g. in model config:
```json
{
  "serve.batch_size": 1,
  "serve.max_gen_tokens": 128,
  "runtime.slot_reserve_fraction": 0.08
}
```

mike: paste from the worker when it OOMs — KV allocation failure during decode (fragmented):
```
[2026-02-28T14:22:03Z] ERROR worker-3: alloc_kv_cache failed: cannot allocate 18446744073709551615 bytes
[2026-02-28T14:22:03Z] INFO worker-3: current slots: 48 used, free runs: 2, frag_ratio: 0.68
[2026-02-28T14:22:03Z] WARN worker-3: falling back to partial-evict policy
```

hannah: we ran a small eval vs fp16 baseline for the same prompt set — quant int4 has avg ROUGE-L -1.2 and MRR down 0.9 points, but latency/token is 2.1x faster. quality hit is small but visible on our high-sensitivity queries. worth running A/B with live traffic sample.

julia: thanks. did an experiment: batch_size=1 + max_gen_tokens=128 cut the OOMs to near-zero in 12h canary, but p50 latency jumped ~45ms. tradeoff looks acceptable for now. note: some long-convo tests still see degraded coherence after quant.

sam: for fragmentation root cause, try two things in parallel: 1) enable incremental KV trimming after each turn, 2) test an alternative quant backend (gptq-lite) that produces smaller per-layer buffers. patch suggestion:
```yaml
runtime:
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.65
  kv_trim_interval_ms: 200
  quant_backend: gptq-lite
```

mike: I'll drop a small reproducer that simulates long chat with many short turns — should stress KV churn. also collect pgrep/malloc stats.

hannah: let's also flag this for eval team: run the critical prompt set and the high-sensitivity user flows under the int4 canary and record quality deltas and tail-latency. put acceptance thresholds (ROUGE-L >= -1.5, MRR delta <= -1).

ci-bot: deploy canary harpoon14b-v2-int4 to pool canary-3 at 2026-02-28T15:00Z — fixture tests passed.

julia: timeline/proposal: 1) run reproducer + host alloc logs (mike) 2) run quant backend swap A/B (sam) 3) eval run on critical prompts (hannah) 4) if quality within thresholds, keep batch=1 + max_gen_tokens=128 as interim default and schedule kernel/allocator work to reduce frag. will update thread with results. :white_check_mark:
